newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota hospital patient killed by injection.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota hospital patient killed by injection.

text.p: A lethal dose of the drug often used to execute criminals by injection was accidentally administered to a 61-year-old hospital patient who died, hospital officials said Thursday.
John Ose died Tuesday shortly after receiving the concentrated dose of potassium chloride, a drug that in a more diluted form is used medically to slow a rapid heart beat.

"The death was caused by potassium (chloride), administered in error by a registered nurse," Michael Lang, vice president at Duluth's Miller-Dwan Medical Centre, said. "We are reviewing what happened so we won't repeat it."
Ose, who was a patient at the hospital suffering from an undisclosed ailment, was given the lethal dose through an intravenous drip in his arm.
